keyRules: In the open category, the maximum height is 120 m, measured as the distance to the closest point on the ground — not simply straight down, so near a slope the adjacent ground may also count. In addition, lower height limits may apply in some areas; these can be found on the drone map. Within a 50 m radius of an artificial structure, you may fly up to 15 m above the structure with the permission of the person or entity responsible for it.

You must register as a drone operator if your drone weighs 250 g or more (or can transfer more than 80 J of kinetic energy in a collision) — this also applies to toys. Below 250 g, registration is still required if the drone has a sensor capable of collecting personal data, unless it qualifies as a toy under the EU Toy Safety Directive. Pilot training/certificate requirements are separate and depend on the drone's class and subcategory.

In Estonia, the minimum age for remote pilots is 16 years — exceptions apply to C0-class drones in subcategory A1, to privately built drones weighing less than 250 g, and when flying under the direct supervision of a pilot who meets the requirements.

In the open category, you must keep the drone within your direct, unaided visual line of sight (glasses/contact lenses are fine; binoculars or a screen do not count) — or fly with the help of an observer, maintaining continuous, clear and effective communication with them so that together you can monitor the airspace and avoid collisions. Follow-me mode is a separate exception, permitted up to 50 m from the pilot.
Do not fly over assemblies of people. Rules for uninvolved persons depend on subcategory, class mark and operating conditions; check the official matrix.
In the immediate vicinity of airports, the height limit in the open category is 0 m — flying is only possible with a specific category operational authorisation.
Night flights are permitted if the drone has a flashing green light (UAS.OPEN.060(2)(g)).
Tallinn Airport CTR: Check it carefully on Estonian Drone Map
Restricted areas around the airports on the islands (Saaremaa, Hiiumaa)

A restricted area has been established near the state border (up to 300 m above ground or water level): flights there may only take place with a permit from the Politsei- ja Piirivalveamet (PPA) (Vabariigi Valitsuse korraldus nr 229, points 3.2 and 5.3). The PPA also establishes temporary restricted areas near the border — check NOTAMs. Strong GPS interference occurs in the border area.
importantNotes: Registration costs 10 € per year and is valid in all EU/EASA countries
The Tallinn Airport CTR covers a significant area

Drone flights are strictly restricted in the Russian border area: there is a complete ban in the Ida-Viru County border zone, a nighttime flight ban along the eastern border, and a risk of GPS interference. Always check the Estonian Drone Map and NOTAMs.
Estonia has a well-developed digital registration system
The GDPR applies when you take photos or videos of identifiable people
